samples.summary: Peer-supplied `listLevel` is still read through a bare `Number(...)` with no clamp; the new `levelOf()` normalizer only protects the planner, so a poisoned level keeps reaching raw sinks (unbounded `String.repeat` in the markdown serializer, NaN/huge geometry in layout and PDF)
samples.evidence: The new module documents the threat itself (`packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:19-27`: "a peer's Tree attribute is read straight through `Number(...)`") and claims "Normalizing at the single point of read is what keeps both guards total". That is only true inside `planListLevelChanges`. The actual read boundaries are unchanged and unclamped: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` (`block.listLevel = Number(attrs.listLevel)`) and `packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243` (same line, used for revision previews). Attack: a principal with write access to a shared doc (collaborator, or an API key with write scope via `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content`, which does not validate `listLevel` — see the companion finding) stores `listLevel: 1e9` (or `1e400` → `"Infinity"`). Every other reader then deserializes it verbatim. Sinks reached with the raw value: `packages/docs/src/serialize/markdown.ts:140` `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` → 2e9-char allocation or `RangeError: Invalid string length`, crashing `wafflebase docs content get --format md` (`packages/cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`) for anyone who exports the document; `packages/docs/src/view/layout.ts:494` `LIST_INDENT_PX * ((block.listLevel ?? 0) + 1)` → NaN/Infinity `marginLeft` that collapses or blanks the rendered document; `packages/docs/src/export/pdf-painter.ts:377` → NaN/huge coordinates into pdf-lib. Note the adjacent `headingLevel` is clamped at its sink (`markdown.ts:156 clampHeadingLevel`) while `listLevel` is not. This is a persistent, other-user-affecting availability/data-integrity issue, not merely a local render glitch.
searchedFor: grep listLevel across packages/docs, packages/frontend, packages/backend, packages/slides

samples.summary: The docs content PUT validator checks every block-style numeric is finite but never validates `listLevel`, so the API is an unvalidated injection point for the out-of-range/non-finite list levels the new planner's normalizer exists to defend against
samples.evidence: `assertValidBlock` (packages/backend/src/api/v1/docs-content.controller.ts:429-511) validates `id`, `type`, `style` shape, `style.alignment` against an allowlist and every `BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS` entry as a finite number (:399-407), and `assertValidHeaderFooter` even validates `marginFromEdge` as finite (:331-339) — but nothing checks `listLevel`. `buildBlockNode` then persists it verbatim: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178` `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`. So `PUT /api/v1/workspaces/:w/documents/:d/content` with `{blocks:[{id:"a",type:"list-item",listLevel:1e9,inlines:[],style:{}}]}` is accepted by an authenticated write-scoped caller and lands in the CRDT for every collaborator, where the readers cited in the companion finding consume it raw (`'  '.repeat(1e9)` in the markdown serializer → RangeError/GB allocation; NaN geometry in layout). The clamp exists in exactly two places today — the clipboard parser and the new `levelOf` in `model/list-level.ts:29-33` — and neither is on this path. `MAX_LIST_LEVEL` is now an exported model constant, so the same bound is trivially applicable here (`@wafflebase/docs` is already imported by this controller at :44-49).

samples.summary: `changes.push(...planSiblingGroup(...))` spreads an attacker-influenceable-length array into a call, which throws `RangeError` past the engine argument limit — inside `doc.batch()`, aborting the whole Yorkie update
samples.evidence: `planListLevelChanges` accumulates one `ListLevelChange` per block in every moved subtree and flushes each group with argument spreading (`list-level.ts:139`). A document containing more than ~65k–125k list items in one sibling array (reachable through the unvalidated `PUT .../content` endpoint, which imposes no block-count limit, or by a malicious collaborator) makes a single Ctrl+A + Tab throw `RangeError: Maximum call stack size exceeded` from inside `doc.batch()` (`packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3605`). `Doc.batch` re-reads and rethrows (`model/document.ts:146-153`), so the gesture surfaces as an uncaught editor error rather than a no-op. Availability only, and requires a very large document, hence low confidence; `for (const c of group) changes.push(c)` removes it.

samples.summary: Subtree coverage and selection membership are keyed by `block.id`, but block ids are not unique-checked on any ingestion path (the CRDT reader defaults a missing id to `''`), so a crafted document can make one indent gesture write to unintended blocks
samples.evidence: `planSiblingGroup` dedupes with `covered.has(block.id)` / `selectedIds.has(block.id)` (list-level.ts:87,90) and the appliers then write by id (`doc.setBlockType(change.block.id, ...)` in editor.ts:1607, text-editor.ts:2729, text-box-editor.ts:831). Uniqueness is not enforced anywhere untrusted: the backend validator only requires `typeof id === 'string' && length > 0` (docs-content.controller.ts:434) and never checks for duplicates, and the CRDT reader assigns `id: attrs.id ?? ''` (`packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:230`), so every id-less node collapses onto the same key. With duplicated ids a selected item can be skipped as "already covered" while `setBlockType(id)` resolves to the first matching block, moving a block the user never selected. Impact is document mangling by a peer-controlled payload, not privilege escalation, so low.
searchedFor: grep setBlockType call sites in the diff

samples.summary: The rewritten `indent`/`outdent` still write through the raw `docStore` (`docStore.snapshot()`) inside a batch on the read-only-wrapped `doc`, so the only thing keeping a viewer session out of this new multi-block write path is the `MUTATING_METHODS` name list
samples.evidence: Read-only mode is enforced two ways: `readOnlyDocStore` neuters the store behind `doc` (`editor.ts:1076`) and `MUTATING_METHODS` overwrites the API surface (`editor.ts:4488-4504`, which does list `indent`/`outdent`). The new bodies mix the two stores: `doc.batch()` goes through the neutered proxy — whose `batch` trap deliberately *runs* the body (`store/read-only.ts:104-112`) — while `docStore.snapshot()` (editor.ts:3606, 3625) targets the un-wrapped store. Today unreachable for a viewer because `indent`/`outdent` are neutered, but this is exactly the fail-open shape #989 was about: a rename or a new list-level entry point that forgets the name list reaches a store write with no `readOnly` check of its own. `guardedSetPageSetup` (editor.ts:3274) shows the intended defence-in-depth (`if (readOnly) return;`) — the same one-line guard belongs at the top of `applyListLevelChanges` / `indent` / `outdent`.

verdict.reason: Every element of the finding is present as described. `yorkie-doc-store.ts:495` and `crdt-tree.ts:243` both read peer-supplied `listLevel` through a bare `Number(...)` with no clamp. The new `levelOf()` normalizer (`list-level.ts:29-33`) is module-private and used only by `subtreeOf`/`planSiblingGroup` (`:50,:56,:92,:102`); only `planListLevelChanges` is exported, so it protects nothing outside the indent/outdent planner — its own comment at `:99-101` concedes the layout pass reads `listLevel` raw. The raw value reaches `markdown.ts:140` `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))`, which has a floor but no ceiling (unbounded allocation / RangeError), while the adjacent `headingLevel` IS clamped at its sink by `clampHeadingLevel` (`markdown.ts:156-160`) — confirming the asymmetry the reviewer cites. Geometry sinks `layout.ts:494`, `table-layout.ts:93`, `pdf-painter.ts:366-377,589`, `peer-cursor.ts:254,392` also consume it raw. The write side persists it unvalidated (`docs-tree.ts:178` `String(block.listLevel)`), and the markdown export is reachable from the CLI (`cli/src/docs/content.ts:129`). I searched for any clamp/validation on the deserialize boundary or at these sinks and found none, so no already-guarded ground applies. Untrusted, persisted, cross-user input driving unbounded allocation and NaN/Infinity geometry is unsafe input handling within the security lens, not merely a local render glitch.

verdict.reason: Verified independently: the docs PUT validator has no listLevel check anywhere. assertValidBlock (docs-content.controller.ts:429-512) validates id/type/style and delegates to assertValidBlockStyle, which covers alignment (:385-398), BLOCK_STYLE_NUMERIC_FIELDS as finite numbers (:399-407) and AUTHORED_SPACING_FIELDS as booleans (:418-426); assertValidHeaderFooter even bounds marginFromEdge (:331-339). listLevel is never inspected. No other gate covers it: the handler takes `@Body() body: unknown` (:158) so the global ValidationPipe (main.ts:65-66) has no DTO to apply, and the only listLevel occurrences in packages/backend are the raw writer (yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 `attrs.listLevel = String(block.listLevel)`), its spec, and a seed builder — no clamp. The value round-trips raw through the shared reader (packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 `Number(attrs.listLevel)`) and the frontend store (yorkie-doc-store.ts:494-495), and consumers use it unbounded: markdown.ts:140 `'  '.repeat(Math.max(0, block.listLevel ?? 0))` (RangeError / multi-GB string for 1e9), layout.ts:494 and table-layout.ts:93 multiply it into geometry, doc-canvas.ts:599-602 indexes with it. The only clamps in the repo are the clipboard parser (packages/docs/src/view/clipboard.ts:348-351) and the new levelOf (packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33, MAX_LIST_LEVEL at :7), neither reachable from the writer path. No OpenAPI/schema layer exists. In lane as unsafe input handling: a write-scoped caller stores a tiny value that is amplified into a crash/allocation blow-up for every other reader of the shared CRDT document.

finding.summary: The MAX_LIST_LEVEL ceiling now fails open for non-finite / out-of-band `listLevel` values, so a level poisoned via the unvalidated collaborative ingest path lets a normal indent gesture push items past the ceiling without bound and write `NaN` levels across a whole run of neighbours.
finding.evidence:
Both new guards are plain comparisons against a value that is never validated to be a finite number:
- `subtreeOf` line 37: `if (nextLevel <= level) break;` — if the root's `listLevel` is `NaN`, every comparison is false, so the "subtree" swallows the entire following run of list-items instead of stopping at the first same-or-shallower one.
- `planSiblingGroup` line 74: `if (delta > 0 && deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL) continue;` — `deepest = Math.max(deepest, NaN)` is `NaN`, and `NaN >= 8` is false, so the refusal is skipped and line 79 writes `(listLevel ?? 0) + 1` for every member.

Concrete chain: a collaborator (only needs edit access to the shared doc) sends a Yorkie tree block attribute `listLevel: "foo"` (attrs are stringified on the way out at packages/backend/src/yorkie/docs-tree.ts:178 and parsed with a bare `Number()` on the way in at packages/docs/src/model/crdt-tree.ts:243 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:495 — no `Number.isFinite`, no clamp). The victim's document now holds `listLevel = NaN` on that block. When the victim puts the caret on it and presses Tab / Cmd+], the two guards above both fail open, so: (a) the poisoned item's own level is written back as `NaN`, (b) a following child that was legitimately at level 8 is written to 9, and repeated presses drive it to 10, 11, … past the documented ceiling, and (c) the walk carries an arbitrarily long run of unrelated items. verdict.reason: The finding describes both guards as plain comparisons against an unvalidated `listLevel`, but the repository routes every read through a normalizer. packages/docs/src/model/list-level.ts:29-33 (`levelOf`) returns 0 for any non-finite value (`!Number.isFinite(raw)`) and otherwise clamps to [0, MAX_LIST_LEVEL] via Math.min/Math.max/Math.floor. The quoted guard at :57 operates on `levelOf(next)` (:56) versus `levelOf(blocks[index])` (:50), so a NaN root reads as 0 and the subtree walk stops at the first same-or-shallower sibling instead of swallowing the following run. `deepest` is accumulated only from normalized values (:52, :59), so it can never be NaN and the ceiling check `deepest >= MAX_LIST_LEVEL` at :94 cannot fail open — an out-of-band level clamps to 8 and indent is refused. The write is `levelOf(blocks[j]) + delta` at :102, not the claimed `(listLevel ?? 0) + 1`, so no NaN or unbounded level is ever written back; text-editor.ts:2722-2732 applies only that normalized plan value. Existing tests at packages/docs/test/model/list-level.test.ts:127-162 pin exactly the claimed NaN / Infinity / past-ceiling / negative vectors. The cited line numbers (37/74/79) land on comment text in the actual file, indicating the evidence was quoted from code that is not present in this working tree.
